claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start with: **Do you have a child or children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. Alex is 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions.

**Are you responsible for Alex?** By this I mean, does Alex live with you, and are you the person who is mainly responsible for their day-to-day care (such as providing food, clothing, and looking after them)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't live with me. He lives with his dad. But I do help out - I contribute about £10 a week towards his clothes and things like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. This is important information.

**Does anyone else currently receive Child Benefit for Alex?** For example, does Alex's dad (or anyone else Alex lives with) claim Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I don't believe his dad is claiming Child Benefit for Alex, no. As far as I know, nobody else is getting it for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Just to clarify the living arrangements:

**Is there any shared care arrangement where Alex stays with you for part of the time?** For example, does Alex spend certain nights of the week or weekends living with you, or does he live full-time with his dad?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex lives with his dad full-time. He doesn't stay with me at all - I just help out financially when I can with the £10 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why: To qualify for Child Benefit, you must be "responsible" for the child. This means the child must normally live with you, and you must be the main person providing their day-to-day care (such as feeding them, making sure they have clothes, and looking after them generally).

Since Alex lives full-time with his dad and doesn't stay with you at all, you don't meet this requirement. While it's great that you contribute £10 a week towards his expenses, financial contributions alone don't qualify you for Child Benefit when the child doesn't live with you.

However, Alex's dad may be eligible to claim Child Benefit if he is responsible for Alex's day-to-day care. If he's not currently claiming it, he might want to look into whether he's eligible.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
